description: FLUID SQL/1 conformance vectors (forge-cli RFC-data-rules.md section 2.9). They define the language: every implementation (forge-cli's validator, flux-expr/2) parses, checks and evaluates every vector and reaches its verdict, tree, canonical text, type, scale and values. Each vector names a model, one expose: models[name] = {columns: {name: {type, enum?, placeholders?: {values?, prefixes?}}}, relationships?: {name: {to: <model>}}, validityWindow?: true}, where type is the FLUID column type as a contract writes it and validityWindow says the expose declares a validity window, so no path may reach it through a relationship. A vector also names a site: predicate (check, when, aggregate.filter: the text must be a bool, and a NULL result counts as FALSE) or value (expr). With derive, the text is the expr of a derive on that column and must fit it. A refused vector gives one reason from reasonCodes and has exactly one defect. An accepted vector gives its tree (one node per construct; see nodes), its canonical text, its type and, for a number, its static scale (an integer, or unbounded), and eval cases: a row (column -> value), the links (relationship -> the row it reaches, or null for none; a relationship left out reaches none) and the result. A column left out of a row is NULL.
encoding: No JSON number appears anywhere in this file: numbers, scales and limits are strings. A number is a decimal string; a result of static scale s is written with exactly s digits after the point, and one of unbounded scale as its shortest decimal, or as p/q in lowest terms when no decimal is exact (1/3). Compare numbers by value. A bool is true or false, a string is itself (compared by code points, never normalized), a date is YYYY-MM-DD, a timestamp is ISO 8601 without an offset, a timestamp with time zone ISO 8601 with one (compare instants), and NULL is null. A float column's value is the shortest decimal that converts back to the double.

limits.measure: The text is NFC-normalized, then measured in code points, and so is its canonical text, which adds a space after each comma: a text whose canonical text would pass 4,096 is refused too (too-long), so every canonical text parses back. Depth: a literal or a column reference is 1; every other construct, and every pair of parentheses, is one more than the deepest thing directly inside it, so a chain of 63 ANDs over 64 names is 64 deep. An IN item, ROUND's places and its mode are literals inside their construct (an IN item -1 is one number literal, depth 1). ROUND takes at most 38 places (founder pick, 2026-11-16).

reasonCodes.too-long: longer than 4,096 code points after NFC normalization, or a canonical text that would be
reasonCodes.comment-or-semicolon: a ';', '--' or '/*' outside a string literal or a quoted name
reasonCodes.syntax: a text the grammar (RFC-data-rules.md section 2.1) does not derive
reasonCodes.round-places: ROUND to more than 38 decimal places
reasonCodes.bad-date: a DATE literal that is not a calendar date from 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31 written YYYY-MM-DD
reasonCodes.multi-link-path: a path over more than one link (rel.rel.col)
reasonCodes.unknown-column: a name that is not a column of the expose, or of the relationship's target
reasonCodes.unknown-relationship: rel.col where rel is not a relationship of the expose
reasonCodes.validity-window: a path through a relationship whose target declares a validity window
reasonCodes.untyped-column: a column whose type has no FLUID SQL/1 type
reasonCodes.type-mismatch: operands or arguments of the wrong type, or a predicate position given something other than a bool
reasonCodes.null-literal: the NULL literal where nothing gives it a type: an IN item, an operand of a comparison or BETWEEN, or every operand of a construct
reasonCodes.enum-literal: a string literal compared with a column whose enum does not list it
reasonCodes.derive-target: a derive target with no FLUID SQL/1 type, a float, or a number without a declared scale
reasonCodes.derive-type: a derived value whose type differs from its target's
reasonCodes.derive-scale: a derived value whose static scale exceeds its target's, or is unbounded
